text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear position against driverless cars from the introduction through the conclusion","quality":"argumentative focus","description":"It maintains a consistent stance and keeps returning to the main claim instead of drifting into broad observations."},{"evidence":"“driverless cars aren't truly driverless” and “add more complexity and management”","quality":"reasoned development","description":"It develops its points by explaining why the article’s technology descriptions weaken the case for driverless cars."},{"evidence":"“This additional feature… adds unneeded complications” and “overly complex and would most likely cost a lot of money”","quality":"analysis of implications","description":"It does more than repeat facts by interpreting what those features would mean for drivers and adoption."},{"evidence":"“Although driverless cars could potentially make transportation easier… right now they are not a good investment”","quality":"nuanced concession","description":"It acknowledges a possible benefit before explaining why the present version still should not be pursued."},{"evidence":"intro questions like “But just because we can create something, does that mean we should?”","quality":"engaging lead","description":"It opens with a more purposeful hook that sets up the argument and frames the issue."},{"evidence":"body paragraphs organized around “one major negative aspect” and “Another negative aspect”","quality":"organization","description":"It structures the essay into clearly separated claims that are easier to follow."}]}
